source: Ed4 C.6.5 to C.6.8, pp.C-71 to C-74; C.7.6.3, pp.C-120 to C-122; corpus-format.md 6.2
description: A transmission with room for one header to the peer carries its top-priority recommendation, not the next entry of the rotation.
note: Table (corpus-format.md 6.1): ladder WN 2, 4, 6, 7 at Long (positions 0 to 3); thresholds measured on WN 2 Long bulk -100, 50, 150, 300 and latency -100, 100, 200, 400; on WN 4 Long bulk -100, 0, 100, 150 and latency -100, 100, 300, 400; on WN 6 Long bulk -100, 0, 300, 500 and latency -100, 200, 400, 600; on WN 7 Long bulk -100, -50, 100, 400 and latency -100, 0, 300, 600; smoothing weight 8, clean run 2, error limit 500 ppt, caps 2 doubling to 8 bursts. Flow as drc-rx-capability-records-ed4 with a 57-byte block: the CAPABILITY burst from 0.0.1.3 ends on WN 6 Long with estimate 150, so MAX-SPEED WN 4 Long and LOW-SPEED WN 2 Long (bulk target 1, latency target 0); mixed, as no SENDER-APPROACH has come (C-0956). The first transmission holds the 35-byte type 7 and two PADDING D_PDUs: 0x8A4, 0x9A2 (top priority, C-0953), then 0x8A4, the first rotation entry. At 60000 conn 1 queues 27 bytes for 0.0.1.3, whose type 7 fills the block alone: one header, which carries the top priority again, 0x8A4, not the next rotation entry (LOW-SPEED, 0x9A2): priority decides use when slots are limited (C-0949, interp C-1260).
